hypotheses.evidence: E-graph equality saturation: rounds-only case converged at round 8 (2,388 enodes, 336 classes, zero final unions) with per-root DP tree costs identical before and after [120, 16, 0, 0, 50, 10, 0, 0] and hill-climb extraction at the baseline 34; joint case hit the class cap at round 5 (35,615 enodes, 7,658 classes) with costs identical [219, 27, 0, 0, 105, 21, 0, 0] and extraction at the baseline 56. Soundness verified inductively: 380,520 enode evaluations, 0 mismatches, anchors 400 trials, 0 mismatches. RAW_RESULTS/exp033_egraph_20261115T110602Z.json; RAW_RESULTS/exp033_egraph_verify_20261115T110717Z.json.
hypotheses.statement: A cheaper graph for the two-round SHA-256 round function (with or without its schedule pair) exists within the word-level rewrite system R1 to R6 (rotation composition and distribution over LUTs and inverse, constant folding, LUT flattening over at most 3 atom classes, add associativity, add(x, 0), add(x, x) = shl, LUT degeneracies; no bitwise-through-ADD rule, none being sound).

hypotheses.evidence: Incumbents proven exact (1,000,000 differentials each, 0 mismatches; z3 UNSAT for both cones; PROOFS/exp033_cone_synth_gates_20261115T114122Z.json). Full-cone CEGIS at L = 5 returned synth unknown at the 600 s solver timeout (82-example seed; RAW_RESULTS/exp033_cone_synth_a_cone_20261115T114616Z.json): inconclusive, not a refutation. Narrowed substantially by H-033-03 and H-033-04; the only unrefuted shapes are H-033-05.
hypotheses.statement: A straight-line program of 5 instructions over V = {ADD, LUT(any imm), ROTR(any k), SHR(any k)} computes a full round cone (a-cone or e-cone), against the proven 6-instruction incumbents.

hypotheses.evidence: CEGIS synthesis at L = 3 UNSAT at iteration 0 on a 34-example seed (a universally correct program would match every example). The 4-instruction incumbent (ROTR 2, ROTR 13, ROTR 22, XOR3 LUT) is proven exact by z3 (UNSAT) and matches on 200,000 differentials, 0 mismatches. Minimum is exactly 4. RAW_RESULTS/exp033_sigma_synth_sigma0_20261115T122610Z.json; PROOFS/exp033_sigma_synth_sigma0_20261115T122610Z.json.
hypotheses.statement: Sigma0(x) is computable in 3 instructions over V given x and up to four arbitrary side values independent of x.

hypotheses.evidence: CEGIS synthesis at L = 3 UNSAT at iteration 0 on a 34-example seed. The 4-instruction incumbent (ROTR 6, ROTR 11, ROTR 25, XOR3 LUT) is proven exact by z3 (UNSAT) and matches on 200,000 differentials, 0 mismatches. Minimum is exactly 4. RAW_RESULTS/exp033_sigma_synth_sigma1_20261115T123152Z.json; PROOFS/exp033_sigma_synth_sigma1_20261115T123152Z.json.
hypotheses.statement: Sigma1(x) is computable in 3 instructions over V given x and up to four arbitrary side values independent of x.

hypotheses.evidence: Shape E1 is EXCLUDED for both cones: for the e-cone by H-033-13 and for the a-cone by H-033-14 (cone-conditioned synthesis UNSAT in both). Two earlier Sigma0 conditioned attempts had timed out at 900 s under heavier contention (RAW_RESULTS/exp033_sigma_synth_sigma0_cone_20261115T124139Z.json and exp033_sigma_synth_sigma0_cone_20261115T125903Z.json) before the successful run. Shape E2 (routing Sigma through the Maj or Ch value, so the Boolean instruction sits inside the Sigma sub-DAG) remains open for both cones: not found, not excluded.
hypotheses.statement: A 5-instruction cone program exists via one of the two shapes the Sigma bound does not cover: (E1) exploiting the correlation s = T1 + T2 inside the Sigma sub-DAG, or (E2) routing the Sigma output through the Maj or Ch value.
hypotheses.exp042_update_2026_11_15: Appended 2026-11-15 by EXP-042 (Phase 002 step 5); the original statement and evidence above are unchanged. Shape E2 is now REFUTED for both cones at the stated bounds: straight-line programs over V, cone length 5, the sum s produced by a single ADD of the two sum inputs, the Boolean output produced by a single LUT instruction. Method: if the Boolean instruction lies inside the Sigma dependency DAG, the DAG minus it is a program of length at most 3 over the pool (s, p, q, x, y, m) with m = Maj(s, a, b) resp. Ch(s, e, f) given free per cone-realizable example; CEGIS synthesis at L = 3 over that pool returned UNSAT at iteration 0 for the a-cone (540.3 s, 16 examples) and the e-cone (214.0 s, 16 examples), z3 5.4.1, host AMD EPYC 9D25. With shape E1 already excluded by H-033-13 and H-033-14, no 5-instruction cone exists via E1 or E2 at these bounds, and the cone minimum over V is exactly 6 under them. Out-of-bounds shapes (sum or Boolean output produced by two or more instructions) are not covered by this refutation; the full-cone CEGIS at L = 5 remains inconclusive there (EXP-042 added timeouts at 1,500 s and 1,400 s on a 22-example seed), so H-033-02 stays open in that residual generality only. Full record: research/sha256d/exp042/EXP042_REPORT.md.

hypotheses.evidence: Re-derived from the taint boundary (nonce is W3, first consumed in round 3; W18 first nonce-dependent expanded word). RAW_RESULTS/exp033_taint_20261115T110152Z.json, accounting block. Stated as conventional accounting only; explicitly NOT a lower bound on any implementation.
hypotheses.statement: The conventional SHA-256d implementation computes 67 of 192 round slots per template (64 first inner block plus rounds 0 to 2 of the second) and 125 per nonce (61 remaining inner rounds plus 64 outer rounds).

hypotheses.evidence: 100,000 of 100,000 random samples each, and z3 UNSAT on the negation with fully symbolic template words for both. PROOFS/exp033_taint_proofs_20261115T110152Z.json.
hypotheses.statement: The schedule delta identities D(W18) = sigma0(nonce) and D(W19) = nonce hold exactly for all templates and nonce changes.

hypotheses.evidence: z3 UNSAT on the negation for both words; consistent with the taint map (state nonce-free after 3 rounds, dependence first appears in a and e after round 4). PROOFS/exp033_taint_proofs_20261115T110152Z.json.
hypotheses.statement: After 3 rounds of the second inner block, state words a and e are integer-affine in the nonce with slope 1.

hypotheses.evidence: Refuted by a z3 SAT counterexample (n1 = 539234578, n2 = 1283462784), numerically re-verified: D(n1 xor n2) = 43171369, D(n1) xor D(n2) = 3724592575, not equal. PROOFS/exp033_taint_proofs_20261115T110152Z.json.
hypotheses.statement: D(W20) is GF(2)-linear in the nonce delta, so the schedule admits a linear representation past W19.

hypotheses.evidence: Digest taint census: 48 of 48 computed schedule words digest-dependent, 64 of 64 rounds produce digest-dependent words, 0 digest-independent complete rounds. RAW_RESULTS/exp033_taint_20261115T110152Z.json, outer_digest_taint block. Independently confirms the EXP-027 census.
hypotheses.statement: Some part of the outer SHA-256 compression is digest-independent and can be precomputed before the inner digest exists.

hypotheses.evidence: Consumption census: every produced word is consumed bitwise in the very next round (a' by Sigma0 and Maj; e' by Sigma1 and Ch) and arithmetically 3 rounds later (a' as the addend in e_new = d + T1; e' as the h addend in T1). No bitwise-free window exists. RAW_RESULTS/exp033_taint_20261115T110152Z.json, consumption_census block.
hypotheses.statement: A redundant (for example carry-save) representation of a produced state word can defer resolution across the round boundary because a bitwise-free window exists.

hypotheses.evidence: Every outer digest word depends on all 64 outer rounds (H-033-10 census), and the compared most significant word is a feed-forward sum over the final state; no proper prefix of the outer rounds determines any digest word, so no partial verdict exists. Analysis in MATHEMATICAL_INVESTIGATION.md section 3.4.
hypotheses.statement: Comparing a partial outer digest against the target can abandon a trial before all 64 outer rounds complete, saving rounds.

hypotheses.evidence: Cone-conditioned CEGIS synthesis at L = 3 UNSAT at iteration 0 on a 16-example seed, with operand pool (s, T1, T2, a, b), s = T1 + T2 enforced per example, every example cone-realizable, and every sub-DAG instruction counted including side-value intermediates. The e-cone Sigma sub-DAG therefore has at least 4 instructions unconditionally. RAW_RESULTS/exp033_sigma_synth_sigma1_cone_20261115T131822Z.json; PROOFS/exp033_sigma_synth_sigma1_cone_20261115T131822Z.json.
hypotheses.statement: Sigma1(e') is computable in 3 instructions over V by a sub-DAG that exploits the correlation e' = d + T1 (the produced word's own summands as separate operands).

hypotheses.evidence: Cone-conditioned CEGIS synthesis at L = 3 UNSAT at iteration 0 on a 16-example seed, with operand pool (s, T1, T2, a, b), s = T1 + T2 enforced per example, every example cone-realizable, and every sub-DAG instruction counted including side-value intermediates. The a-cone Sigma sub-DAG therefore has at least 4 instructions unconditionally. RAW_RESULTS/exp033_sigma_synth_sigma0_cone_20261115T132821Z.json; PROOFS/exp033_sigma_synth_sigma0_cone_20261115T132821Z.json.
hypotheses.statement: Sigma0(a') is computable in 3 instructions over V by a sub-DAG that exploits the correlation a' = T1 + T2 (the produced word's own summands as separate operands).
